analysis: Both changed files are docs only; no executable code, config or deployment changes. docs/architecture/security/encryption.md head lines 121-122 add a claim that a delta checkpoint names its parent only through a keyed commitment, so files of one conversation stay unlinkable without the cache key. This is a documentation claim about a new incremental-checkpoint feature whose implementation (SSDBlockStore / DBK3 metadata, delta checkpoint parent commitment) is not in the supplied evidence. It is consistent with T-041 (HMAC-keyed names, no prompt-derived metadata beyond keyed tags in DBK3 AAD) only if the commitment is truly keyed under a KEK-derived key. T-041 detection_hint and the reference doc ssd-kv-cache.md#dbk3-file-format should be checked: a new AAD/metadata field for a parent commitment falls under the 'DBK3 metadata fields or AAD construction' review trigger, and the threat model entry may need updating. Also the doc says the format is no longer 'unchanged', and the incremental mode could widen at-rest observable metadata (delta file count and sizes may leak conversation-turn structure, which is traffic analysis, not prefix confirmation). docs/developer/test.md changes (lines 627-629) only extend a benchmark report description and mention DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0 as a baseline toggle; no security control change. The incremental-checkpoint code is outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm the keyed commitment, whether it is domain-separated and salt-scoped (T-041 point d), or whether the toggle default affects at-rest exposure. Recommend a review of the corresponding Swift cache changes. No findings qualify from the supplied docs alone.
